docs.summary: Hands the most recent block of audio from the audio thread to the game thread, for meters, scopes and spectrum displays.
docs.remarks: One writer and one reader, and the writer never waits. Both used to take the same lock, which meant the audio thread could block behind the game thread copying the whole buffer out: the game thread stalling is a slow frame, the audio thread stalling is an audible dropout. Instead the writer bumps a counter either side of the copy, odd while it is mid-write. The reader takes the counter, copies, and takes it again: unchanged and even means it saw a whole block, and anything else means the writer overtook it, so it retries a few times and then reports nothing new. Missing an occasional block is invisible in a visualiser, which is all this feeds.

docs.summary: Copies as much of `src` as fits and returns how much that was. Anything past the capacity is dropped rather than written past the end of the array, which is what happened when the destination was sized from the source and so bounds-checked itself.

Copies the samples written by the last [`Write`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.Audio.AudioBuffer~Write) into `output`, growing it to hold them if it is too small, and returns how many are valid. Returns 0 when the writer kept overtaking the read, meaning there is nothing consistent to show.
